result.headline: Cells fell pack-wide to 2.5 V while BMS SOC stayed high; undervoltage trip opened contactors at t=2100.5 s.
result.explanation: The BMS under-voltage protection opened HV. Upstream, the SOC overstated charge by about 56 pp. The data cannot separate SOC estimation error, low usable capacity and under-read current; a capacity test or BMS history would confirm which.

evidence.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=1698.5 s: 45.2 -> 30.8 % (step -14.4, 9x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The SOC was abruptly re-stated while measured current stayed 6.95 A. Charge accounting finds 32.74 pp unexplained (56.8 -> 24.0 % in 29 s, 0.056 Ah measured).

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.cell_voltage[min] changed level for good at t=640 s: median 3.2 before, 2.864 after V (2240x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Cell voltage fell far earlier than any protection. The highest cell fell too (line 23), so the decline is pack-wide while the SOC still read about 58 %.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT battery.pack_current held 6.95 from t=0 to 2100 s (4201 samples)
evidence.shows: Current is perfectly flat for 2100 s. Counted charge was only about 4.1 Ah against the 60.4 Ah promised by the starting SOC, which fits an under-reading or saturated current channel as one candidate.
Fault level rose 1 -> 2 -> 3 (t=1453, 1799, 2100.5 s). Both contactors opened at the same instant (lines 19-20), so the order fits a protective response.

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.soc[bms] changed level for good at t=240 s: median 60.4 before, 58 after % (120x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Between corrections the SOC followed measured charge (ratio 1.036 and 1.291), so the estimator was counting charge with no visible voltage-based correction.

checked.check: Charge accounting: SOC change against integrated pack current
checked.result: SOC tracked measured charge / 100 Ah between corrections. One 32.74 pp step is unexplained, needing about 4065 A where 6.95 A was measured.
checked.about: SOC estimation error, usable capacity and current under-read all predict this

checked.check: Energy shortfall: delivered charge against the SOC promise
checked.result: About 4.1 Ah was delivered against 60.4 Ah promised. That needs a 56 pp SOC overstatement, or about 7 Ah usable capacity, or current under-read about 14.9x.
checked.about: SOC estimation, usable capacity, current under-read

checked.check: Cell-level pattern: weak cell against pack-wide decline
checked.result: Lowest cell was index 81 in 100 % of samples. The highest cell fell 450 mV against a 260 mV spread at the trip, so the whole pack was depleted.

checked.check: Sensing fault: smoothness and rest rebound
checked.result: Lowest-cell samples never jumped more than 1 mV. Cells rebounded at rest to 2.28-2.59 V by t=2400 s. This is the pattern of a real cell, but no inspection was done.

checked.check: Order of events: contactor or VCU fault first
checked.result: Fault levels 1 and 2 came before the contactors opened. They opened 0.0 s after level 3, so the order does not fit a contactor-first fault.
No earlier cases (lessons empty). The plan says telemetry cannot separate the three upstream causes: documents, an independent meter or a capacity test are needed.
checked.about: SOC estimation, usable capacity, current under-read

effects.why: Protective escalation after cell under-voltage. It explains how HV was lost, not why the cells were that low.
Contactor opening is the consequence of fault level 3.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a4 t=680 s: battery.pack_voltage[pack] changed level for good (307.7 -> 281.9 V) (see line 26; strength 7.506)
effects.why: Pack voltage follows the cell voltage decline and does not point to a separate fault.

safety_findings.statement: Violation: 32.74 pp SOC re-statement not explained by measured charge. Treat the SOC as unreliable until the upstream cause is found.
Review: 3 escalations recorded with no specification to judge them against. The protection is the machine acting as designed, not the cause.
HV was not re-closed after the shutdown. Cells rested at 2.28-2.59 V, so any HV closure or charging needs a rest-voltage check by a trained technician first.

unknowns: Whether the SOC was calibrated at a full charge, and when, since the machine was last charged.
The cell chemistry, series count and under-voltage thresholds, which are needed to judge the trip sequence.
Whether the pack_current channel is genuine: it is perfectly flat at 6.95 A for 2100 s and its sensor accuracy is not stated.
